description:
Task: Harmonize MODIS/VIIRS Hot Spots.     Problem: Satellite drift breaks tracking.   Solution: Web app mapping data into an accurate activity calendar.
I'm the Data Lead (Python). Seeking: Frontend (React/Maps), Backend (FastAPI/Docker), Designer (UI/Video). 
No satellite background needed. Data pipeline mapped out. DM me!
summary:
FireHarmony is a web app that harmonises MODIS and VIIRS active-fire hotspots into one consistent monthly burning-activity calendar for the Punjab–Haryana crop-burning region, 2012–2025. Users pick an area by preset, grid drag or map click, and the calendar flags unusually high and low months. The monthly data for any area can be downloaded as a CSV. VIIRS is the reference record, built from NASA FIRMS data.

It addresses the challenge by showing where comparisons between satellites and years break down. Daytime detections in October–November fell about 90% from 2021 to 2025 (91,523 to 9,126), while Aqua’s daytime pass drifted from 13:48 to 15:12 and night detections stayed low. This is consistent with burning moving to times between satellite passes, which our data cannot prove on its own.
details:
FireHarmony is a web app that builds one consistent monthly burning-activity calendar from MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspots for the Punjab–Haryana region, 2012–2025. MODIS and VIIRS count fires at different pixel sizes and overpass times, so their records can’t simply be compared.

How it works: we use NASA FIRMS hotspots (vegetation fire, daytime, confidence filters), summed monthly on a 0.25° grid. VIIRS S-NPP is the reference. Users pick an area by preset, grid drag or map click. The calendar flags months above the 90th or below the 10th percentile, and the area’s data can be downloaded as a CSV.

Key finding: October–November daytime detections fell 90% from 2021 to 2025 (91,523 to 9,126), while Aqua’s pass drifted from 13:48 to 15:12 and night detections stayed low (361 to 490). This is consistent with burning moving to times between satellite passes, which our data cannot prove on its own.

We show failed tests on purpose: the month-by-month model (about 60% error), a fixed Aqua factor (up to 43% overshoot) and forecasts all failed, so none is offered. The pre-2012 bridge is validated but not loaded.

Tools: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind, Recharts, MapLibre; Python (pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, duckdb).
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
